science.title: Circular near-field mapping of microwave magnetic fields using a projection-based diamond fiber probe
science.description: Accurate characterization of microwave (MW) near fields is essential for antenna diagnostics and electromagnetic engineering, yet conventional probes primarily access linear components and provide limited polarization information. Here, we demonstrate a fiber-integrated diamond probe based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV⁻) centers for projection-based mapping of MW magnetic fields with circular selectivity. The measurement exploits transition-selective coupling between Zeeman-resolved spin transitions and circular components of the MW magnetic field defined with respect to the NV quantization axis, such that the observed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast reflects a projection onto a spin-defined circular basis rather than the field magnitude. This framework enables a physically consistent description of polarization-dependent response in near-field environments without a unique propagation direction. Operating in a continuous-wave regime, the probe provides robust measurements without absolute calibration and yields spatial distributions directly comparable with simulations. Measurements of a double-ridge horn antenna show agreement with linear field distributions, while mapping of a helical antenna reveals circularly selective response consistent with local measurement geometry. These results are performed using practical antenna structures relevant to wireless communication systems, establishing a compact, quantum-enabled platform for polarization-sensitive microwave diagnostics in realistic electromagnetic environments.

science.title: Lateralized behaviour of dairy cows and calves during nursing and suckling
science.description: Parent–offspring interactions play an important role in offspring survival. Although there is evidence that these interactions are predominantly guided by the right hemisphere, little is still known about the factors that shape this lateralized processing. This study therefore aimed to explore lateralized behaviour of dairy cows and calves during nursing and suckling, respectively, focusing on the development during the first days after birth and the effects of calf sex, dam parity, and allosuckling. Video observations were made of the calf suckling and dam nursing behaviour of 59 group-housed dam-calf pairs from birth to four days after. Calves showed a significant bias to initiate suckling from the left side. Analysed separately, only males showed a significant left bias to initiate suckling. Furthermore, daily analyses showed that calf suckling and dam grooming during nursing were significantly left biased on the first day only. Although nursing interruptions by the cow were also left biased on the first day, most of the findings suggest that left lateralized dam-calf interactions could be associated with heightened maternal care. Such knowledge could help to identify appropriate maternal behaviour in livestock production systems that rely on maternal investment to raise healthy offspring, like cow-calf contact systems.
